body.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\), the explicit local-polynomial learners satisfy \(\mathsf G_n\). In particular, \(\mathfrak B_n=O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n)\) and therefore \(n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n=O_P\{n^{5/6-2\beta}(\log n)^{5/2}\}=o_P(1)\) because \(\beta>5/12\); bounded foldwise empirical increments give \(\sqrt{\log n}\,\mathfrak R_n=o_P(1)\); and the smooth plug-in estimates give \((\log n)\mathfrak K_n=o_P(1)\) and \(|\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)-1|=o_P(1)\). More generally, whenever \(\mathsf G_n\) holds and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), optimized-value stability gives \(\{S_n-S_n^{\circ}\}/a(T_n(P))=o_P(1)\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\).
body.justification: This separates the actual product, local empirical, variance-normalization, and clock thresholds required at the moving Gumbel level from the stronger instrumental assumptions used to verify them.
body.gap: Published pointwise causal-isotonic LR theory requires a nuisance product small relative to one cube-root neighborhood; the displayed conditions add the logarithmic accuracy needed after scanning order \(n^{1/3}\) dependent neighborhoods.
body.consumer: The lemma lets later work replace the local-polynomial implementation by any learner collection that verifies the same four quantitative remainders.
